en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighteenth Chapter
Regarding the discourse on the teaching of the Dhamma:
Should it not be said that "the Dhamma was taught by the Blessed Buddha"?
“Yes. “By whom was it taught?
“It was taught by a magically created being.”
Is the Jina, the Teacher, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, the Lord of Dhamma, the Refuge in Dhamma, a created being?
You should not say so… [and so on]… It should not be said.
“Was the Dhamma taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One?”—
“Yes.”—
“By whom was it taught?”
"It was taught by the Venerable Ānanda.
"Is the Venerable Ānanda the Conqueror, the Teacher, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, the Lord of Dhamma, and the Refuge in Dhamma?
"One should certainly not say so... [and so on].
Is it not to be said that "the Dhamma was taught by the Blessed Buddha"?
Yes, it is.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
"In brief, Sāriputta, I might teach the Dhamma;
in detail, Sāriputta, I might teach the Dhamma"?
“Sāriputta, whether I teach the Dhamma in brief or in detail,
those who understand it are rare.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” [you reply].
“In that case, the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One.
It should not be said thus.
“Has the Dhamma been taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One?”—
“Yes.”—
“Was it not said by the Blessed One:”
“Bhikkhus, it is with direct knowledge that I teach the Dhamma, not without direct knowledge;
it is with its basis that I teach the Dhamma, not without its basis;
it is with its demonstration of efficacy that I teach the Dhamma, not without its demonstration of efficacy.”
Monks, when I teach the Dhamma through direct knowledge and not without direct knowledge, when I teach the Dhamma with its basis and not without its basis,
and when I teach the Dhamma with its demonstration of efficacy and not without its demonstration of efficacy, my exhortation should be heeded and my instruction should be followed.
And it is enough for you, monks, to be satisfied, enough to be elated, and enough to be joyful.
“The Blessed One is a perfectly enlightened one; the Dhamma is well-expounded; the Saṅgha is practicing the good way.
And while this exposition was being spoken, the ten-thousandfold world system trembled.
Is there such a sutta? Yes, there is.
“Yes.
“In that case, the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One.
The Discussion on the Teaching of the Dhamma is finished.
